title: Three-pillar focus scratchpad — Q1 personal OKRs
content:
Context: quick scratchpad for Q1 personal OKRs and weekly check-in template. Purpose is to keep a small, repeatable loop to avoid scope creep, capture micro-experiments, and maintain energy. This is intentionally messy — notes to self, questions, and mini-demos.

Top-level thesis: focus drives compounding output. I want 3 measurable pillars this quarter that map to work outputs, learning, and health. Each pillar gets 1–2 KPIs and 2 supporting habits. Weekly check-ins are 15 minutes max.

Pillars (draft)
1) High-impact execution (ship quality features faster)
   - KPI: reduce average PR cycle time for my ownership area from 5.6 days to <=3.5 days by quarter-end (measure: PR merged date - PR opened date; exclude infra/deploy-only churn).
   - Output targets: 3 medium features (customer-visible) + 1 reliability improvement landed.
   - Supporting habits: daily 45m deep-work block (9:30–10:15), weekly PR tidy-up session Friday 30m.
   - Quick notes: need to coordinate with platform team for CI flakiness (JIRA-PLAT-842). Consider a temp rule: if no review in 48h, ping reviewer on Slack and add a light reviewer fallback.

2) Model serving craftsmanship (learn & apply inference optimizations)
   - KPI: complete 2 hands-on experiments demonstrating >=1.2x throughput improvement on an internal benchmark (latency-sensitive workload) with readme and replication steps.
   - Output targets: experiment runbook + one short tech note for team + code changes in a feature branch.
   - Supporting habits: 2x 90-minute lab sessions (Tue/Thu afternoon), keep an experiment log (this doc).
   - Quick notes: pair with Mikael for kernel selection heuristics; link to PR #623 for baseline.

3) Sustainable energy (avoid burnout, maintain cognitive bandwidth)
   - KPI: maintain >=7.0 average sleep score (Oura metric) and <15% missed deep-work blocks per month.
   - Output targets: consistent morning routine, weekend wind-down 90 minutes of no-email.
   - Supporting habits: morning walk + 10m planning, hard stop at 6:30pm (except emergencies).
   - Quick notes: track sleep in weekly check-in bullet; ask Aisha for short guide on asynchronous boundaries.

Weekly check-in template (15 minutes)
- Week range: ______
- Wins (1–3 bullets): what shipped, measurable signals (metrics), small wins that matter
- Blockers / asks (1–3 bullets): who to ping, tickets to unblock, decisions needed
- Experiment status (1 line per experiment): hypothesis, current measurement, next step
- Habit score (1–10): sleep / deep-work / exercise; variance notes
- One improvement for next week (tiny, timeboxed)

Example (week of 2026-03-02)
- Wins: removed duplication in caching layer (reduced 95p latency by ~9% on dev harness); PR opened for canary routing fix; experiment baseline captured.
- Blockers: CI flake still causing slow merges (JIRA-PLAT-842); need capacity from infra to run long-endurance experiment.
- Experiment: batch-size scheduling — hypothesis: dynamic batch sizing will reduce tail latency on mixed sequence lengths. Current: prototype shows 1.1x throughput but +12ms tail; next: test with KV cache warmup.
- Habit score: sleep 7.2, deep-work adherence 82% (missed Mon morning), exercise 3x/ week.
- Improvement: block Wed 13:00–14:30 for experiment runs.

Mini-retro (monthly)
- What went well: smaller PRs worked better; Friday tidy sessions drop context-switch cost.
- What to change: clearer pre-PR checklist (CI/Lint steps, test matrix) + more pairing on infra-y tickets.
- Risks: ramp fatigue if I overcommit lab sessions while shipping features. Mitigation: cap lab time to 3.5 hours/week; use async notes for repeatable steps.

Mini-experiments (log)
- Experiment A: auto-batcher prototype (Jan 28–Feb 10) — result: 1.15x throughput on homogeneous inputs; doc in /platform/experiments/auto-batcher. Next: integrate with KV cache simulation.
- Experiment B: small-quant quantization (Feb 5–Feb 26) — result: +0.9x throughput but perceptible quality drift on long prompts. Decision: hold for now; revisit with eval set.
- Experiment C (planned): routing policy fallback — measure SLO hit-rate under simulated outage. Who: pair with Mikael. Timeline: Mar 15–Mar 30.

Parking lot / questions to resolve
- How strict should PR size limits be for cross-team dependencies? (tradeoff: bigger PRs reduce coordination overhead but increase review burden)
- Can I get an infra test node for long-duration workloads? Follow-up: @mikael on Slack.
- Should I log habit scores in a simple sheet for trend analysis? Might be useful to correlate with throughput days.

Action items (this week)
- [ ] Draft pre-PR checklist and add to my repo's CONTRIBUTING.md (target: Wed)
- [ ] Schedule 90-minute block Tue/Thu for experiment runs and invite Mikael (target: today)
- [ ] Short tech note: write 1-page summary of batcher prototype (target: Fri)
- [ ] Ping infra about test node; link JIRA-PLAT-842 to request (target: Mon)

Notes to self (loose)
- Be ruthless about scope: if a task will take >8 hours, split into 2 tickets.
- Keep one-sentence objectives for each PR so reviewers know the intent quickly.
- If habitual blocks slip 2 weeks in a row, reduce commitments by 25% and re-evaluate.

Random thoughts / drafts
- Potential OKR phrasing: "Improve delivery velocity and reliability in my ownership area while building repeatable inference experiments that push 1.2x throughput without SLO regressions."
- Consider a weekly public-internal thread (short Slack post) summarizing 2 lines — helps async visibility and keeps momentum.

End of scratchpad. Revisit at end of month for consolidation and convert to formal OKR doc if two pillars show traction.
